summary: Iteration 8 full-stack test of the 4 new features + bio correction. Backend regression: 64/64 pytest passing (backend unchanged this round). Frontend (mobile 390x844): SVEGLIA IMPASTI works (permission grant, toast 'Sveglie attivate', green state, reset+reschedule on recompute, no console errors); FORNO NEL PIANO works exactly as specced (ventilato shows temp-20 with fan note, statico shows full temp with static note, no card when no oven selected); PIANO IN PDF works (real .pdf download 'piano-settimanale-mikilab.pdf', 3-button row, warning toast on empty plan); bio corrected in IT and DE. LOTTI DIVISI is only PARTIALLY working: the 'N tornate' badge and the >60' over-proof warning render correctly, but the interleaving does NOT actually reduce the waiting time of short-rest doughs - the schedule with maxChunk=30 is byte-identical to maxChunk=999. Regression verified: weekly add/save/persist after reload, sd-load-day prefill from plan (12 pz), Quando infornare compute+persist, oven CRUD (create statico+ventilato, delete), AI chat (LLM answered in IT). All test data cleaned up.

integration_issues.issue: Splitting into rounds has no effect on the schedule. Repro: start 03:00, row A = 5000 pz / 4 s-pz / rest 0 / mix 15, row B = 20 pz / 4 s-pz / rest 30 / mix 15. With sd-maxchunk=999: B waits 319' and is formed 09:04-09:06 (⚠️ over-proof). With sd-maxchunk=30: identical output (B still 09:04-09:06, attesa 319'), the only difference is the cosmetic '12 tornate' label on A. The stated benefit (short-rest doughs formed between chunks to cut the over-proof wait) is not delivered.

issues: For a split batch the 'Formatura' range is printed as formStart-formEnd (e.g. 03:30-09:04) which hides the fact that the work is done in 12 separate rounds; showing the per-round slots (or total forming minutes) would make '12 tornate' actionable.
sd-maxchunk accepts any string (including empty / 0 / negative); it is clamped in code (max(1,...)) but the input has no min attribute so the UI can display an invalid value.

action_items: Fix the forming-station scheduler in StartDoughs.compute(): candidates.sort((a,b)=>a.c.ready-b.c.ready) is plain FIFO and, because every chunk of a dough shares the same `ready` timestamp, all chunks of the earliest-ready dough are always consumed before any other dough - so chunking never interleaves. Use a priority that reflects urgency, e.g. among ready chunks prefer the dough with the smallest total formMin (shortest-job-first) or round-robin one chunk per dough per pass, or EDF on (ready + tolerance).
Optional: render the individual round slots (or total forming minutes) for a split dough instead of a single formStart-formEnd span.
Optional: add min="5" / step to sd-maxchunk.
critical_code_review_comments: StartDoughs.compute(): the chunk loop is O(n^2) over chunks (5000 pz @4s with maxChunk=30 -> 12 chunks, fine, but maxChunk=1 on a big batch creates 334 chunks and a 334-iteration scan each pass). Acceptable now, but cap chunk count or use a heap if maxChunk can be 1.

enableAlarms(): if notification permission is denied, ok=false and only an in-tab toast+beep is scheduled, yet the UI still turns green and says 'Sveglie attivate' - user gets no hint that OS notifications will not appear. Consider a distinct message when permission is denied.
enableAlarms() relies on setTimeout, so alarms silently die on reload/tab close (documented by the dev, but no UI hint). A short note under the button would avoid a missed bake.
PianificaProduzione: the fan -20°C adjustment is hard-coded in the JSX; extract to a constant (e.g. FAN_TEMP_DELTA) shared with any future oven logic.

WeeklyPlan.pdfPlan() uses jsPDF helvetica (WinAnsi) - IT/DE accented chars render fine, but if recipe names ever contain non-Latin-1 chars the text will be mangled; also the y-overflow guards (275/280) duplicate logic that could be one helper.

rca_of_the_issue: LOTTI DIVISI: in StartDoughs.compute() every chunk pushed for a dough carries the same `ready` value (it.readyToForm). The scheduler picks candidates whose ready<=cursor and sorts ascending by `ready`, so the dough with the earliest readyToForm always wins every tie/comparison and all of its chunks are drained consecutively - reproducing exactly the pre-chunking FIFO schedule. Splitting therefore only changes the `rounds` counter (display) and never yields the forming station to a dough that becomes ready later, which is precisely the over-proof case the feature was meant to solve.
